Last night I am at Noodles & Company with my wife and kids, and I order a Japanese Pan Noodles.

This is a pretty healthy dish as long as you don't bathe it in some kind of bullshit MSG laden beetus juice, which they do by default. Fortunately, I can order this dish "bare" which means without the sauce, which is exactly what I do.

So the poor teenager at the register looks forlorn as I order "a small Japanese pan noodles, bare." He has to call over the manager: the smallfat, pimple faced, 21 year old manager of this shift of Noodles & Company. Teen asks how to input that order. She addresses me, and says something like this:

Oh, I'm sorry, we only have the bare pan noodles in regular size.

Regular size is enough to feed a small elephant. I look at her appropriately; that is to say that I stare her down like it was the dumbest thing I have ever heard. I've heard dumber, but this becomes a contender.

After staring for a moment, dumbfounded and mouth agape, I reply:

Are you telling me that you can't fill a smaller bowl with the same ingredients?

To which she answers with her best customer service tone:

We can put in the smaller bowl but we'd still have to charge you for the regular... but the regular has more of everything! More veggies and all that good stuff.

Again, I stare blankly at her for another 30 seconds. I am giving her time to revisit the words that she just spoke to me.

Sensing that I am not going to accept this nonsense, the dark truth reluctantly comes forth:

We don't have that order in the POS system, because we are afraid the small size of this dish isn't filling enough when it's bare.

My stoic expression is instantly replaced with the rage of a thousand swells. The force of a thousand clicks on /v/fph/ boiled inside me. I stifle a mixture of hopeless gasp and maniac laughter as I break.

Fine. Make it a regular then, with a side of a to-go box.

I retreat to fill our water cups while my wife pays. Unbeknownst to me, they give us some kind of military or senior discount to remedy this absurd lapse in corporate judgment and I end up paying less for a regular than I would have for a small.

At Noodles and Company, a server brings your food to the table. To my glee, the smallfat serves us. I delight in unbroken eye contact with Ms. "That's not filling enough" as I waste no time shoveling half of my dish into the takeout box. She waits for a reply to the "anything else I can do for you" trope until I am finished halving my food into two human sized meals, at which point I fake a smile and say, "no, thank you. This will be plenty."

TL;DR - small version of dish without beetus sauce is not even in the point-of-sale system at Noodles & Company because it's "not filling enough."
